CIRCLES / DESIGN REVIEW / 28 OCTOBER 2026

A strong visual system, with a broken guest Join path.

Keep the coral, warm paper and sage identity. Prioritise the guest membership defect and web accessibility semantics, then improve mobile content density and naming.

18production route files reviewed
64saved screen/state captures
7 + 3confirmed gaps / design recommendations
1high-priority functional defect
Prioritised findingsEvery screenScreenshot gallerySuggested sequence
Coverage is explicit. Every production route was opened at 320 × 740 and 390 × 844. The five public content routes also received 768 × 1024 and 1440 × 1000 checks. The internal Theme Lab and shared dialogs were reviewed separately. Private routes were captured at their guest gates and their signed-in branches inspected in source. This is an audit of the current local web preview, not a signed-in iOS/Android certification.

What is working

Visual consistency

Editorial headings, rounded cards, restrained action colour, generous spacing and photography create a coherent identity. Shared controls and loading/error treatments are substantially more consistent than the older audit baseline.

Measured layout

0 document-width overflows in the captured states. 0 visible control frames under the app’s 44 × 44 target in the sampled viewports. These measurements do not cover offscreen controls, native hit-slop or every authenticated state.

Useful recovery

Search no-results states, invalid chat/report links and the OAuth callback error give understandable recovery routes. Guest gates do not reveal private records. Dialog keyboard focus entered the Close control and a visible focus outline was observed.

Contrast improvements retained

Core ordinary text now uses the darker secondary token and primary actions use a deeper coral-family fill. The computed opaque-background text sample found no contrast failures. This limited sample excludes gradients, image overlays, inputs, opacity and unrendered states; it is not a blanket accessibility pass.

Prioritised findings

1 High · 6 Medium · 3 Low. Seven confirmed/source-supported defects or accessibility gaps and three design recommendations. Environment blockers are listed separately.

A01 · HighConfirmed defect

Guests cannot use Join: the button spins indefinitely

Circles, Discover circle cards, Circle detail

Rendered at 320 and 390 pixels; also reproduced in tablet/desktop public views. Join is disabled and busy before any action. For a guest, both pendingJoinScope and circleScope are null, so their equality incorrectly reports an active request. Circle detail repeats the same comparison.

Recommended change. Require a non-null pending scope before treating the operation as busy. Keep the guest Join action available so it can open sign-in. Check the related chat pending comparison without relaxing account-scoping safeguards.

Done when. As a signed-out visitor, Join has a readable label, no spinner, and opens sign-in. As a signed-in member, only a real in-flight operation disables it. Test account changes and late responses.

A02 · MediumConfirmed accessibility gap

Selected tabs and filters are visual only in the web preview

Bottom navigation, feed filters, Discover categories, circle sections; other accessibilityState consumers need the same compatibility check

On Home, the selected Home tab and For you filter have no aria-selected, aria-pressed or aria-current attribute. The accessibility tree does not expose a selected item. Source supplies accessibilityState, but the installed react-native-web mapping reads separate ARIA/accessibility props instead of that object.

Recommended change. Add a cross-platform control contract that actually exposes selected/pressed/current state on web while retaining native semantics. Use tab selection for real tabs and pressed state for toggle buttons. Audit busy/checked state through the same adapter.

Done when. DOM and accessibility-tree checks identify exactly one current navigation tab and the selected filter. Verify changes after keyboard activation; check VoiceOver/TalkBack separately.

A03 · MediumConfirmed accessibility gap

Most visual screen titles are not semantic headings

Home, Discover, Circles, circle/profile detail, Messages, Create, onboarding and most guest gates

The 390-pixel DOM captures contain zero headings on these screens despite prominent visual titles. Account Email and the OAuth error screen provide working counterexamples with heading roles.

Recommended change. Introduce a shared screen-title component with native header semantics and web heading levels. Give major sections a logical hierarchy, without making the wordmark another page heading.

Done when. Each screen has a useful primary heading and logical section headings. Screen-reader heading navigation reaches the screen title, main content sections and dialog title.

A04 · MediumConfirmed accessibility gap

Browser pages have no human-readable document title

Web preview: Home and public profile directly checked; route metadata needs app-wide coverage

document.title is an empty string on Home and /person/2. Browser tab labels fall back to localhost URLs. Existing tab navigation options do not provide meaningful document titles for these rendered pages.

Recommended change. Set page titles such as Home · Circles, Discover · Circles and Jules Park · Circles through the supported Expo Router head/metadata path. Include useful titles for loading, error and private screens.

Done when. Titles change correctly on direct links and client navigation and remain meaningful in browser history and assistive technology.

A05 · MediumConfirmed accessibility gap

Dialogs lack an accessible name

Comment sheet directly inspected; sign-in dialog also needs an explicit title association

The rendered comments modal has role=dialog and aria-modal=true, but neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby. Its visible title The conversation is plain text. Its close control is announced simply as close. Sign-in has a visible heading but the outer Modal has no explicit title association.

Recommended change. Name each dialog from its visible title and give close controls contextual names such as Close comments. Preserve the observed focus containment and keyboard focus indicator.

Done when. The accessibility tree announces Comments or Sign in as the dialog name. Keyboard focus enters, stays within the dialog and returns sensibly when dismissed. Recheck on both native platforms.

A06 · LowSource-confirmed affordance mismatch

The desktop search advertises an unimplemented shortcut

Wide shared header

The search button displays ⌘ K. No app keydown/shortcut listener was found in app, components, lib or hooks. This audit did not claim a browser-level shortcut test.

Recommended change. Implement and test the advertised shortcut with the platform-appropriate label, or remove the badge. Keep click/tap search working.

Done when. The displayed shortcut opens and focuses Discover search on the relevant platform, and does not conflict with editable fields.

A07 · LowConfirmed copy defect

Single-item counts use plural copy

Circle cards, Circle detail, public profile statistics/end-of-list

Existing records render 1 members, 1 moments and All 1 moments loaded. The desktop recommendation row already uses a singular/plural distinction, so the same data is described inconsistently.

Recommended change. Use shared count formatting for member/members and moment/moments, including zero, one and larger counts. Use the same helper in visible and accessible labels.

Done when. Counts of 0, 1 and 2 read naturally across cards, profiles, detail pages and accessible labels.

R01 · MediumDesign recommendation

Bring actual communities higher on small phones

Circles browsing; Home header can receive the same density review

At 320 × 740, the circle banner, search, category rail and directory tabs leave only a small sliver of the first circle image above the bottom bar. This is content prioritisation, not document overflow or a navigation overlap defect.

Recommended change. Reduce the banner height on narrow phones or make it dismissible after the first visit. Retain the identity and editorial copy while giving the directory and its first community more room.

Done when. The initial phone view shows enough of a real circle card to communicate what can be browsed, while search and navigation remain easy to use.

R02 · LowDesign recommendation

Use consistent names for communities and content

Desktop navigation, Circles directory, Discover, composer, profiles

Desktop says My circles for a route that defaults to discovery; mobile says Circles. Content is called Posts in Discover/composer and Moments in profiles and feed copy.

Recommended change. Use Circles for the general directory and Your circles for the membership view. Choose one primary content noun, or deliberately explain the relationship between a post and a moment.

Done when. Navigation and screen labels match the destination at phone and desktop sizes; users do not need to learn two names for the same object.

R03 · MediumDesign recommendation

Replace engineering language in the live lobby with user guidance

Live lobby footer

Visible product copy discusses Native WebRTC, a development or release build and a TURN relay. These are implementation details rather than a practical next action for a person trying to join a live conversation.

Recommended change. Keep camera/microphone expectations clear, detect unsupported environments where possible and show a plain-language next step. Move build and relay requirements to operator/developer documentation.

Done when. A nontechnical person can understand whether live is supported and what to do next without knowing WebRTC or TURN.

Shared design recommendations

  • Retain the identity. No wholesale rebrand is indicated by this audit. Keep decorative bright coral separate from accessible text/action colours.
  • Use a small component contract. Standardise screen headings, selected controls, named dialogs, count copy and busy feedback at the shared component level.
  • Make phone content earn its space. Keep horizontal rails as intentional scrolling regions; reduce promotional space rather than shrinking text or touch targets.
  • Keep recovery actionable. Prefer a clear explanation and a next step over protocol, provider or infrastructure terminology.
  • Protect the native review. Check real keyboards, large text, safe areas and live video on devices before drawing conclusions about native behaviour from browser captures.

Suggested implementation sequence

  1. Fix A01 first. Add the missing non-null guard, cover guest and account-transition cases, and visually verify Join opens sign-in without making a membership write.
  2. Fix A02–A05 together. Expose selected/busy/checked state, semantic headings, route titles and dialog names through tested shared web/native adapters.
  3. Polish A06–A07 and R01–R03. Resolve the shortcut badge, singular counts, mobile banner size, terminology and live guidance.
  4. Complete authenticated validation. Supply the original authorised authentication configuration and use an approved account to review editors, private chat, moderation, Updates and live states. This is a follow-up requirement, not a claim of completed coverage.

Environment and verification limits

  • Supabase public content is connected. Local email sign-in reports that it is disabled. No account or session was fabricated and no permissions were bypassed.
  • No posts, messages, memberships, reports, read states, preferences or broadcasts were created or changed for this audit. No database migrations or seeding ran.
  • Only guest gates were rendered for private screens. Profile editing, saved content, populated conversations, onboarding steps, manager controls, authenticated Updates and active live video were source-reviewed only.
  • Native camera/microphone permissions, actual WebRTC, VoiceOver/TalkBack, hardware safe areas, enlarged system text and physical-device keyboard behaviour remain unverified.
  • Transient loading, empty live listings, starter-content dates, intentional horizontal rails and source-cropped photos are not counted as confirmed design defects. Screenshots can contain brief image loading/fade states.
  • Audit-only work produced reports and captures. Product source is unchanged from Git HEAD db15a9a. The local preview adapter remains in work/.

Reference checks

The report distinguishes the app’s comfortable 44-pixel control target from the WCAG AA minimum of 24 pixels with exceptions. Ordinary text contrast uses 4.5:1 and large text uses 3:1. See W3C contrast guidance, W3C target-size guidance and W3C focus guidance. These spot checks are not a complete WCAG conformance evaluation.
